assessment.nobel_worthiness: Controlled, coherent transfer of quantum states between light and matter (single atoms in cavities, atomic ensembles, quantum memories and elementary network nodes) is the enabling interface for quantum networks and repeaters. The idea is clear and general, and it has become a standard architecture across atomic, solid-state and ion platforms. My own work is on optical quantum memories in rare-earth crystals, so I judge this from close familiarity and note that closeness explicitly.
assessment.attribution: Kimble (network vision and early cavity-QED/ensemble demonstrations), Rempe (single-atom cavity quantum-network nodes and photon-atom state transfer) and Lukin (ensemble storage and slow-light/EIT-based memories, plus later nodes) form a defensible trio. Other groups contributed in ensemble memories and in solid-state memories, so the boundary of the discovery is somewhat soft.
assessment.maturity: Roughly two decades of independent confirmation by many groups and platforms; elementary quantum-network links are demonstrated. A full repeater-based network is not yet realised, but the underlying interface physics is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: The candidate is a compound field (cavity QED, ensemble memories, solid-state memories); a prize may need to fix a narrower core.
Rare-earth-crystal and other memory platforms are not represented in the credited names; I declare my own field's closeness and have not independently verified priority claims.
Practical scalable networks remain a future prospect.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstrations reaching the 10^-18 level, redefined achievable precision in measurement. It yields tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. Clear, original and of broad lasting effect.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and made early demonstrations; Ye drove the ultimate precision and systematic control, using the stabilised laser and comb technology developed with others. Hall and Hänsch were recognised in 2005 for the comb, so this pair is a clean complement. Other strontium/ytterbium groups contributed, but the two named are central.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs now reproduce 10^-18 performance and compare clocks; interpretation is stable. Redefinition of the SI second is pending, which would make recognition timely.
uncertainties: Whether the Academy prefers to wait for the redefinition of the second.
Contributions of other clock groups (e.g. ytterbium, trapped-ion optical clocks) are outside the credited pair.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise clean, tunable many-body Hamiltonians: the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, quantum gas microscopy and simulation of Hubbard-type physics. The concept (Zoller and collaborators' proposal; Greiner and Bloch's experiments) has become a mature platform linking AMO and condensed matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Five names are credited, so a trio must exclude Cirac and Esslinger, both substantial (Esslinger for the fermionic Hubbard realisation). I choose Zoller for the theory, Bloch for breadth of experiments and Greiner for the Mott-insulator and microscopy work, but the allocation is genuinely contestable and overlaps with B011.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation worldwide for over twenty years; the field is mature. Quantitative advantage over classical simulation on hard problems is still being established.
uncertainties: Credit for the Mott transition between Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger, and the theory share of Zoller versus Jaksch and others not on the list, is unresolved.
Overlap with B011 means only one of the two should be prized in a single year.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brings strong single-photon coupling into superconducting circuits, providing the architecture for dispersive readout and gates in superconducting quantum processors. A clear, original, widely adopted invention.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin and Schoelkopf with colleagues (Wallraff and others not listed) proposed and demonstrated the architecture; the trio supports a fair split between theory and experiment, but Wallraff's 2004 demonstration is a notable omission from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Very well confirmed and extended across many labs. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, which makes timing for a closely related follow-on a judgement call.
uncertainties: Overlap with recent recognition of superconducting circuits may reduce the case.
Omission of Andreas Wallraff from the credited names limits attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for a trapped-ion quantum computer, together with later proposals for quantum simulation, defined how controllable atomic systems can implement quantum information protocols. Highly original and influential for AMO quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: The pair is a natural, compact theory-led configuration; the experimental realisation was by Wineland's group and others (partly recognised in 2012). Zoller also appears in B001, so combined consideration is needed.
assessment.maturity: Proposals have been confirmed experimentally many times over thirty years; the interpretation is stable. Theory-only recognition is possible but less usual for the Prize.
uncertainties: Whether a purely theoretical prize is preferred over one including experimental realisers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light below the shot-noise limit, proposed for interferometry by Caves, demonstrated experimentally, and now routinely used in gravitational-wave detectors. A direct example of quantum optics improving the limits of measurement.
assessment.attribution: Caves for the proposal, Kimble for early experimental squeezing (with colleagues such as Slusher, Wu and Kimble's group not all listed), and Schnabel for the practical injection in GEO600. Mavalvala is also credited but I would omit her to keep a three-person limit. Credit for the first squeezing observation is shared with others not in the names.
assessment.maturity: Operational in LIGO/Virgo/GEO600 for years; confirmation is strong and recognition is timely, though the 2017 prize already honoured gravitational-wave detection.
uncertainties: Credit for the first experimental squeezing is spread over several groups.
Kimble also appears in B003, making combined allocation awkward.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry enables ultra-sensitive inertial, gravitational and fundamental-constant measurements. It combines laser cooling, coherent beam splitting and precision readout, and is a major platform for quantum sensing.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard (early matter-wave interferometry), Bordé (theory and Ramsey-Bordé interferometer) and Kasevich (precision gravimetry and gyroscopes) are plausible. Chu was recognised in 1997 for laser cooling, and Chu and others also contributed to interferometric methods, so overlap with prior recognition is possible.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with field applications and many independent groups; fundamental tests are ongoing and not yet at transformative sensitivity for new physics.
uncertainties: Overlap with 1997 and 2001 recognition in cooling and condensates.
Priority among interferometer designs is spread over several groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a field of tunable correlated and superconducting moiré systems; the Bistritzer-MacDonald theory predicted the flat bands and the experiments confirmed the correlated states. A clear and broad influence on condensed matter physics, outside my own field.
assessment.attribution: The theory prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald) and the experiments (Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators, including Cao and others not credited) form a reasonable configuration; the three named people are the natural trio.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly replicated by many groups, though the field is still maturing and the origin of the superconductivity is debated; timing may be early.
uncertainties: Understanding of the superconducting mechanism remains incomplete.
I assess this outside my own expertise and rely on general knowledge, not verified detail.
